# Decifer Reasoning Check — scope

Status: proposed, nothing built. Written 2026-08-19.

A free non-verbal reasoning test: shapes, patterns and sequences, the same kind
of thinking a CAT4 or an 11+ non-verbal paper measures. Sister product to the
[Skills Check](SKILLS_CHECK_SCOPE.md), which covers curriculum attainment. This
one covers reasoning.

---

## 1. The reason to build this ahead of anything else

**Every question can be generated by code, with the correct answer known by
construction.** A matrix, a sequence, an analogy and an odd-one-out are all
functions of shape, count, fill, rotation and size. Generate the rule, apply it,
and the answer falls out. No LLM writes it. No verifier has to check it.

That matters because of the measured state of the existing bank: 10% hard-defect
rate on LLM-generated questions, 72% clean overall, 8,277 published items and a
pipeline that costs money per item. Against that, this product line has:

| | Curriculum questions | Reasoning items |
|---|---|---|
| Where the answer comes from | LLM, then verified | Construction. It cannot be wrong. |
| Defect rate | ~10% on LLM content | 0 by design |
| Cost per item | LLM calls | Free |
| Supply | 8,277, hand-checked | Unlimited |
| Hand-check needed before publishing | Yes, every item | No |
| Curriculum drift risk | Real | None. Reasoning is not curriculum. |

It also sidesteps the content problems in the audit entirely. A generated shape
sequence cannot dress arithmetic in war casualties, cannot cite a picture that
does not exist, and cannot have a distractor that is also correct.

**Second reason:** it finally gives IRT something to calibrate. `lib/irt.ts` has
0 of 8,277 items calibrated on 1,084 lifetime answers. A free, shareable
reasoning test aimed at a market that actively searches for it is the one thing
in this product likely to generate responses at volume.

---

## 2. What it is, and the IQ question settled

**It is a reasoning test.** It measures the same kind of thinking an IQ test
measures: pattern recognition and spatial logic, stripped of taught content.
That is a real and defensible claim, and it is what CAT4 measures too. UAE school
guidance describes CAT4 as having similarities to an adult IQ test.

**It still does not output an IQ score, and must not.** An IQ score, and CAT4's
own SAS score, are norm-referenced: they place a child against a large
standardised sample, mean 100, standard deviation 15. We have no such sample.
A number on that scale, produced without one, is invented, whatever the test
measures.

So the split is:

| We can say | We cannot say |
|---|---|
| "Tests the same reasoning skills as an IQ test or a CAT4 non-verbal paper" | "Your child's IQ is 118" |
| "Reached level 4 of 6 on sequences" | "Top 10% of children" |
| "Strongest on matrices, weakest on rotations" | Any percentile or standardised score |
| "24 questions, here is what they got right" | "Above average for their age" |

**There is an honest route to a score, later.** Once enough children have taken
it, we can report "compared with other children who took this test on Decifer",
labelled exactly that way. That is a self-selected sample, not a national norm,
and the wording has to say so. See §9.

---

## 3. The market, and why it is a better SEO bet than the Skills Check

Two live sources of demand, both of which people search for by name.

**CAT4, and it is a UAE-first opportunity.** CAT4 is used by the top British
curriculum schools in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah for admissions, streaming and
KHDA baseline tracking. Children sitting it for Year 7 entry to selective schools
(Dubai College, Repton, Kings, Brighton College, Nord Anglia) typically take it in
Year 5 or Year 6. It has four batteries: verbal, non-verbal, quantitative and
spatial. Parents receive a CAT4 report and mostly do not understand it.

That is the whole opening. We are a UAE company selling to UAE parents, and the
existing guides surface already targets them.

**11+ non-verbal reasoning.** GL Assessment is now the dominant 11+ provider;
CEM stopped offering paper tests from September 2023 and most grammar schools
moved to GL for the 2023-24 season. GL's non-verbal paper is reported as 80
questions in 60 minutes (single source, verify before publishing that figure).
Its question types are the ones in §4.

**Why this beats the Skills Check for traffic:** "year 4 maths practice" is a
vague, crowded query. "CAT4 practice test", "CAT4 scores explained" and
"non-verbal reasoning 11+" are specific, high-intent, and parents searching them
are already about to pay somebody.

---

## 4. Item types

Four for v1. All four are in both the GL non-verbal paper and CAT4's non-verbal
battery, and all four generate cleanly.

| Type | The question | Rule space |
|---|---|---|
| **Sequence** | What comes next in this row of five? | One or more attributes progress: rotation by a fixed step, count going up, fill alternating, size growing. |
| **Matrix** | A 3x3 grid with one cell blank. Which fills it? | One rule across rows, another down columns. |
| **Analogy** | A is to B as C is to what? | A single transformation learned from the first pair, applied to the third shape. |
| **Odd one out** | Five shapes, four share a property. Which is the odd one? | Four satisfy a rule, one breaks it. |

Deferred: cube nets and 3D rotation. They generate, but rendering a convincing
net is a bigger job than the four above and they are a smaller share of the paper.

**Distractors are generated by breaking exactly one rule.** That is the whole
trick, and it is why these are hard in the right way. If a sequence rotates 90°
and grows, the wrong options are: rotated the wrong way but grown correctly;
rotated correctly but not grown; rotated 180°; correct shape, wrong fill. Every
distractor is plausible because each one is right about everything except one
thing. An LLM cannot reliably do this. Code does it by definition.

---

## 5. How an item is made and stored

**An item is a seed, not a row.**

```
item = generate(type, level, seed)   // pure, deterministic
```

Nothing is stored in a content table. The attempt stores `(type, level, seed)`
per question. To mark an answer, the server regenerates the item from the seed
and compares. To re-render a past report, regenerate it again.

Consequences worth stating plainly:

- The correct answer never reaches the browser. The client gets shapes to draw
  and nothing else.
- A bug report is exactly reproducible: the seed is the whole item.
- There is no content table to seed, migrate, moderate, or hand-check.
- Two children never get the same paper, and one child gets the same paper on
  reload.

This satisfies CLAUDE.md §16.5 differently from the rest of the product. The rule
exists so that adding content needs no code change. Here, content is not authored
at all: the generator is the content, and adding an item type is the only thing
that needs code.

**Rendering is SVG**, generated from the same shape model. Self-contained, sharp
at any size, works offline, no image files, no storage.

---

## 6. Difficulty

Six levels, by construction rather than by calibration, because there is no
response data yet:

| Level | What changes |
|---|---|
| 1 | One attribute varies. Big, obvious steps. |
| 2 | One attribute, smaller steps. |
| 3 | Two attributes vary together. |
| 4 | Two attributes, one of them rotation. |
| 5 | Three attributes. |
| 6 | Three attributes with a rule that differs across rows and columns. |

The test walks the ladder: get one right, go up; get one wrong, go down. That is
genuine adaptivity and it needs no calibration data, because difficulty here is a
property of the generator, not an estimate from responses. This is the one place
in the product where adaptive is honest today.

Later, real response data replaces the constructed levels with measured Rasch
difficulties via `lib/irt.ts`.

---

## 7. The test and the report

**The test:** 24 questions, roughly 12 minutes, 6 of each type. Untimed per
question but the time per item is recorded, because speed is half of what these
tests measure.

**Free, before the email** (matching the Skills Check gate decision):
1. Headline: the level reached. "Reached level 4 of 6."
2. Two lines: strongest question type named, and how many types need practice
   without naming them.

**Behind the email gate:**
3. Per-type breakdown: score and level reached for sequences, matrices,
   analogies, odd-one-out.
4. Median time per question, and which types were slowest.
5. Three practice recommendations, one per weakest type, each a link to a free
   practice set of that type.
6. An honest box: what this does and does not tell you, why there is no IQ
   number, what a CAT4 SAS score is and how it differs.
7. Retake in 4 weeks.

---

## 8. Accessibility, stated up front

A non-verbal reasoning test is inherently visual. There is no version of "which
shape completes this matrix" that works for a child who cannot see the shapes.
The product holds a WCAG 2.2 pass, so this must be handled deliberately rather
than discovered later:

- Every shape gets a text description in the SVG (`<title>` and `aria-label`),
  so a screen reader can read "large circle, striped, rotated 90 degrees".
  That makes the test navigable and, for some children, answerable.
- Full keyboard operation, visible focus, 48px targets, no colour-only cues.
  Fill patterns are hatching and dots, never colour alone.
- The page says plainly that this test is visual, so nobody is set up to fail.

---

## 9. Norms, and the honest path to a score

Do not ship a score. Ship counts and levels.

Once the test has enough completed attempts, we can add one comparison, worded
exactly like this: **"Of the children this age who took this test on Decifer,
your child scored higher than X%."** Not a percentile. Not an IQ. Not "above
average". A statement about our own takers, labelled as such.

That is honest, it is genuinely useful to a parent, and it is the kind of thing
we can actually back. Gate it behind a minimum sample per age band, and hold that
threshold in a named constant so it cannot be quietly lowered.

---

## 10. Data model

Small, because there is no content to store.

```sql
reasoning_attempts (id, token, age_band, started_at, finished_at,
                    total_items, raw_score, level_reached,
                    type_results JSONB, profile_id NULL)

reasoning_answers (id, attempt_id, position, item_type, level, seed,
                   chosen_index, was_correct, time_ms)

-- reuses skill_check_leads' shape; the parent's email and nothing else
reasoning_leads (id, attempt_id, parent_email, consented_at, verified_at,
                 deleted_at, source, utm)
```

Same privacy posture as the Skills Check: the attempt holds no personal data, the
only personal field anywhere is the parent's email, and `age_band` is a band, not
a date of birth. Same RLS posture: enabled with no policies, plus REVOKE ALL, all
access through API routes.

Deliberately NOT reusing `skill_check_items`: that table's `question_id` is a
required foreign key to `quiz_questions`, and a generated item has no row to
point at.

---

## 11. Build order and gates

**Phase A — generators.** `lib/reasoning/shapes.ts` (the shape model + SVG),
`generate.ts` (four item types x six levels), pure and seeded.
*Gate:* for every (type, level), 1,000 generated items each have exactly one
correct option, four distinct options, and regenerate identically from their
seed. This is a property test, not a handful of examples.

**Phase B — one type end to end.** Sequences only. Runner, adaptive ladder,
marking, result page, email gate.
*Gate:* a full run with no login at 375px; the answer never appears in the page
source; a reload mid-test does not reshuffle.

**Phase C — all four types, report, email.** Per-type breakdown, timings,
practice links, Resend report email, delete link.
*Gate:* report renders from seeds alone with no content table; email arrives.

**Phase D — public pages and SEO.** See §12.
*Gate:* pages in the sitemap; no build-time DB query per page.

**Phase E — norms.** Only once the sample supports it. See §9.

---

## 12. SEO

| Route | Target |
|---|---|
| `/reasoning` | Hub. "non-verbal reasoning test for kids" |
| `/reasoning/non-verbal` | The free test itself |
| `/reasoning/cat4-practice` | "CAT4 practice test", "CAT4 Dubai" |
| `/reasoning/11-plus` | "11 plus non-verbal reasoning practice" |
| `/reasoning/r/[token]` | Result page. `noindex`. |

Guides, in the existing `lib/guides/content/` system:

- **CAT4 explained for UAE parents**: what the four batteries are, when your
  child sits it, which Dubai schools use it. Highest-intent page on the list.
- **CAT4 scores explained**: what an SAS of 100 or 115 means, why the mean is
  100 and the spread is 15, what a stanine is. This is where we explain norms and
  say plainly that our own test does not produce one.
- **IQ tests for children: what they measure, and what to use instead.** This is
  how we answer the "IQ test for kids" searches honestly. The page says what an
  IQ test is, why a free online one cannot give a real score, and points at the
  reasoning test as the useful version.
- **11+ non-verbal reasoning: every question type, with examples.** The examples
  are generated by our own generator, which makes this page cheap to build and
  impossible for a competitor to copy at volume.

Cross-link with the Skills Check both ways: reasoning measures how a child
thinks, the Skills Check measures what they have learned, and a parent who wants
one usually wants both.

---

## 13. Not in scope

- Any IQ number, percentile, or standardised score (see §2).
- Verbal and quantitative reasoning batteries. Non-verbal and spatial first.
- Cube nets and 3D rotation items.
- Claiming to predict or replicate a CAT4 result.
- Selling this as 11+ or admissions preparation with an outcome promise.
